cur:manuscripts-lavra-a92-christ-deesis-.summary: Christ stands frontally on a jewelled footstool against a gold ground, blessing and holding a jewelled Gospel book, labelled IC XC; around him medallions show the Virgin and John the Baptist at the top — forming a Deesis of intercession — and the four evangelists below, each named in Greek. The page presents Christ as the Word proclaimed in the Gospels.
facts: Commons dates this Gospel book of the Great Lavra on Mount Athos to the 10th century.
The pairing of the Virgin and John the Baptist on either side of Christ — the Deesis — became one of the central images of Byzantine prayer.

cur:manuscripts-lavra-a92-christ-deesis-.notes: Date (10th century) rests on the Commons description only; could not be confirmed against a catalogue.

cur:monumental-hagia-sophia-southwestern.summary: Against a gold ground in the lunette above the doorway, the Virgin sits on a backless jewelled throne with the Christ Child on her lap, who blesses and holds a scroll. Emperor Constantine, at her left, offers a model of the walled city of Constantinople, and Emperor Justinian, at her right, a model of Hagia Sophia itself. The two founders thus entrust city and church to the protection of the Mother of God and her Son.
facts: The mosaic dates from the reign of Basil II and was rediscovered during the restoration by the Fossati brothers in 1849.
The enthroned Virgin was probably modelled on the earlier mosaic in the apse semi-dome of the church.

links.label: Wikimedia Commons: Southwestern entrance mosaics (Hagia Sophia)

cur:monumental2-faras-noli-me-tangere.summary: Only fragments survive: at the right the white, red-striped robe and bare feet of the standing risen Christ, with his hand extended, and at the left the red-mantled figure of Mary Magdalene bending low before him; above, parts of a haloed head and another white garment remain. Even in ruins the encounter in the garden – the first appearance of the risen Lord – can be read in the contrast of the upright Christ and the kneeling woman.
facts: The museum identifies the scene as the resurrected Christ with Mary Magdalene; it comes from Faras Cathedral, excavated by the Polish expedition in 1961–64.

cur:monumental2-faras-noli-me-tangere.notes: Very fragmentary; identification follows the National Museum in Warsaw. Date range straddles AD 1000.

cur:objects-otto-imperator-ivory-milan.summary: Christ sits enthroned between St Mary and St Maurice, raising his hands over a small imperial family who prostrate themselves at his feet: the emperor, the empress and a little crowned son. The inscription OTTO IMPERATOR runs along the base, and the letters IHS XPS name Christ above. The plaque expresses the Ottonian ideal of the emperor as the humble servant and representative of Christ the true King.
facts: The V&A notes that this relief of Christ enthroned with the Emperor Otto II, his wife and child is stylistically related to the Basilewsky Situla, suggesting both were made in Milan around 980.
The figures are usually identified as Otto II, Theophanu and the infant Otto III, though some have proposed Otto I and Adelaide.
cur:objects-otto-imperator-ivory-milan.notes: The flanking saints are identified by the inscriptions SCA MARIA and SCS MAURICIUS visible on the frame. Image is small (486 px).

walters:71.241.summary: The slender standing Virgin, her head veil carved in careful overlapping folds, holds the Christ Child on her left arm and gazes out into space. The Child, whose head is now lost, reaches toward her breast and holds an apple in his left hand. The sweeping apron of drapery and the free-hanging fold from her sleeve make this an unusually inventive Gothic ivory.
facts: The Walters relates the carving to a group of marble sculptures of c. 1340–1370 with similarly unusual drapery, and attributes it to a Mosan workshop.
The Child's left hand with the apple is an old replacement in wood; the Virgin's crown and the Child's head are missing.
Considerable traces of red paint survive on the back of the Virgin's robe, and a rectangular hole in the back shows it was once fixed inside a shrine.
walters:71.241.notes: Worklist year 800 was a parsing error for '3rd quarter 14th century'.
